subject: stf
title: STF.------PRI.INFO.
description: Diagram in WI-26, the first of two on book p310. (C)STF (source transfer) is crossed with PRI-INFO (primary information). The diagram poses what source transfer requires when crossed with primary information — the question the WI section has been building toward: under what conditions can source transfer carry primary information without distortion? STF → PRI-INFO (the crossing) → T-C-IMP (time continuum implications) → POL-DYM (political dynamics) → TM (terminology of a definition). STF → AFL-DY (affinity dynamics); AFL-DY branches to MT-INFO (music information) → AF-CON (affinity convergence) and MT-INFO → LK-IMP (linkage implications); AFL-DY → CULT-SOLD (culture solidification); AFL-DY → IST-F (isolated focus) → RE-ST (restructuralism). Structural argument: source transfer has two parallel productive lines — primary-information → time-continuum → political-dynamics → terminology (a chain that ends in *naming*), and affinity-dynamics → music-information/culture-solidification/isolated-focus (chains that produce affinity convergence, linkage implications, and restructuralism). Critically, real source-transfer of primary information leads to terminology — which Braxton has named as the western device for capturing alternative work. The second arm, through affinity dynamics, produces restructuralism via isolated focus — the route that *preserves* the source. The diagram thus diagrams the choice point: source transfer can either route into political-terminology or into isolated-focus-restructuralism, but not both. The white improvisor's structural problem is that the institutional pull is toward the first route.
